excelHints.title: Excel tables
excelHints.note: How tables are found in this source's workbooks. Leave a hint on Auto-detect unless a workbook is read wrong.

help.header_rows: The exact number of header rows. Set it when a data row is read as a header, or a header as data.
help.max_header_rows: The most rows read as header rows. 1 means each table has a single header row.
help.table_gap_rows: How many blank rows in a row end a table. Set 1 when tables are separated by one blank row.
help.column_gap: How many blank columns in a row separate tables side by side. Set 1 when one blank column separates them.
help.min_columns: The fewest columns a table has. Set 1 to read one-column tables.
help.min_data_rows: The fewest data rows a table has. A table with fewer is not read.
help.range: The cells this table is, read exactly, such as Sheet1!A3:F200. Quote a sheet name with spaces: 'Q1 results'!A1:D9.

excelHints.entriesNote: A hint here wins over the same hint above. A table is named file__sheet, as it is listed.
excelHints.workbookNameHelp: The workbook's file name, such as report.xlsx.
excelHints.tableNameHelp: The table's name as the source lists it, such as report__summary. With a range, this is the name the range's table takes.
excelHints.repeated: Named twice; give each workbook or table one entry.
excelHints.repeatedFix: Excel tables: a workbook or table is named in two entries. Give each one entry.
